---
title: "Modular architecture"
---

The pipeline should expose the same core operations through Python functions, command-line subcommands, and complete pipeline runs. Each stage should have a narrow contract: inputs, outputs, validation, execution, and report generation.

## Stage contract

Each stage should define:

- Accepted input object types and on-disk paths.
- Required metadata and validation rules.
- Output object type.
- Output folder layout.
- Provenance fields.
- Warnings and hard failure conditions.
- Whether it can stream, must materialise data, or can run lazily.

## Passing objects between steps

The architecture needs to support both in-memory and on-disk execution.

| Mode | Use case | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| In memory | Fast iteration, notebooks, short debug slices. | Pass SpikeInterface objects directly between Python calls. |
| On disk | Long jobs, cluster execution, resumable workflows. | Save stage outputs and reload them from `manifest.yaml`. |
| Hybrid | Expensive partial runs followed by interactive inspection. | Persist selected checkpoints while passing cheap objects in memory. |

## Inter-session processing

Inter-session concatenation and alignment require explicit handling of channels and metadata.

- The default multi-session bad-channel policy should remove the union of all detected bad channels.
- If the user disables the union policy, warn that unit matching and concatenation can become unreliable.
- Inter-session alignment should produce quality metrics and an HTML report before sorting.
- The preprocessing output may be either a single concatenated session for sorting or a list of aligned recordings for later unit matching.

## Further analysis hooks

Each step should output an object that can be used for downstream checking and visualisation. For example, sorting outputs should be usable by drift plots, curation GUIs, and unit-matching tools without requiring the user to rediscover paths manually.

## Architecture questions

- How should step outputs be typed so they work equally well in Python and on disk?
- Should there be one massive config, per-step configs, or a hybrid resolved config?
- Which objects are serialised directly, and which are represented by paths plus metadata?
- How should GUI curation tools write decisions back into the pipeline run folder?
- How much of unit matching belongs in the core pipeline versus a downstream module?
